content: 1. A study published in the Journal of Community Health in 2013 evaluated the effectiveness of lay health worker interventions specifically designed for Cambodian Americans. The intervention aimed to address health disparities and improve health outcomes within this population. 2. Taylor VM and colleagues conducted a study in 2011, published in the Journal of Community Health, focusing on hepatitis B education for Asian immigrants using English as a Second Language (ESL) programs. The study highlighted the importance of culturally tailored educational interventions to increase awareness and prevention of hepatitis B. 3. In 2009, Taylor VM and colleagues evaluated a lay health worker intervention targeting hepatitis B among Chinese Americans and Canadians. Published in the Journal of Community Health, the study demonstrated the potential of community-based health workers in improving hepatitis B screening and vaccination rates. 4. A randomized control study by van der Veen YJ et al., published in Health Promotion International in 2014, examined the impact of culturally tailored interventions to promote hepatitis B screening among Turkish Dutch individuals. The study emphasized the role of cultural sensitivity in public health initiatives. 5. Le Lan C and colleagues, in a 2012 study published in the Journal of Hepatology, explored a multidisciplinary approach to treating hepatitis C in alcohol-dependent patients actively abusing alcohol. The treatment combined interferon and ribavirin, addressing the complexities of managing hepatitis C in this high-risk group. 6. The OPTIMAL study, conducted by the Chronic Liver Disease Foundation in 2014, assessed the impact of physician-directed education on patient compliance with hepatitis C therapy. The findings underscored the importance of physician involvement in improving adherence to treatment protocols. 7. A 2007 study evaluated the compliance of hepatitis C genotype 1-infected patients receiving PegIntron/Rebetol therapy alongside a patient assistance program. The results highlighted the role of support programs in enhancing treatment adherence. 8. Another study in 2009 investigated adherence among patients receiving PegIntron Pen/Rebetol therapy for hepatitis C in conjunction with a patient assistance program. The findings reinforced the value of structured support systems in managing chronic hepatitis C. 9. A separate 2009 study examined the role of psychotherapy support programs in improving adherence to PegIntron/Rebetol therapy for hepatitis C. The integration of mental health support was shown to positively influence treatment outcomes. 10. Renou CLP and Pariente A, in a 2009 study published in Hepatology, analyzed the impact of therapeutic education on the outcomes of chronic hepatitis C treatment. The study highlighted the benefits of patient education in achieving better clinical results. 11. Zhou K and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in 2016, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases, to evaluate interventions aimed at optimizing the care continuum for chronic viral hepatitis. The study provided evidence-based recommendations for improving care delivery. 12. Mwai GW et al., in a 2013 systematic review published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society, examined the role and outcomes of community health workers in HIV care in sub-Saharan Africa. The review highlighted the critical contributions of community health workers in resource-limited settings. 13. Patel V and colleagues, in a 2011 study published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, assessed the impact of lay health worker-led interventions for depressive and anxiety disorders in India. The study demonstrated significant improvements in clinical and disability outcomes over 12 months. 14. Joshi R et al., in a 2014 systematic review published in PLoS One, explored task-shifting strategies for managing non-communicable diseases in lowand middle-income countries. The findings supported the feasibility and effectiveness of task-shifting in addressing healthcare workforce shortages. 15. Kredo T and colleagues, in a 2014 Cochrane review, evaluated the outcomes of task-shifting from doctors to non-doctors for initiating and maintaining antiretroviral therapy. The review provided evidence supporting task-shifting as a viable strategy in HIV care. 16. Glenton C et al., in a 2013 Cochrane review, synthesized qualitative evidence on barriers and facilitators to implementing lay health worker programs for maternal and child health. The study identified key factors influencing the success of such programs. 17. Mandelblatt JS and colleagues, in a 1999 study published in Preventive Medicine, investigated breast and cervical cancer screening among multiethnic women. The study examined the influence of age, health status, and sources of care on screening uptake. 18. Green BB et al., in a 2013 randomized trial published in Annals of Internal Medicine, tested an automated intervention with stepped increases in support to enhance colorectal cancer screening uptake. The intervention demonstrated effectiveness in improving screening rates. 19. Norman J and colleagues, in a 2008 study published in Harm Reduction Journal, evaluated the acceptability and feasibility of peer worker support roles in community-based hepatitis C treatment for injecting drug users. The study highlighted the potential of peer support in improving treatment engagement. 20. The STARD 2015 guidelines, published in Clinical Chemistry, provided an updated list of essential items for reporting diagnostic accuracy studies. These guidelines aimed to standardize and improve the quality of diagnostic research reporting.
